notes: Blender rest coords (head +X, up +Z, +Y = dragon's left). Rest pose = standing, wings spread nearly flat (tip elevation ~5 deg; adult ~28 deg). Wingspan 0.998 is larger than nose-to-tail length 0.746 (adult: 1.0 vs 0.94), so at the same SCALE formula the baby looks wide; pick desiredLength with that in mind. Keys start at frame 0: clip durations are exactly Fly 3.0 s (72 f, 3 flaps + 1 finger-breath), Glide 2.0 s (48 f), Idle 3.0 s (72 f); first and last key identical, every clip keys all 38 bones. Same 38-bone names/topology as fire_adult_anim (GLTFLoader strips the dot: wing1.L -> wing1L). No jaw bone. Head bone runs (0.36,0,0.11)->(0.49,0,0.11); mouth = head-bone head + (0.135, 0, -0.005) in rest pose. Fly/Glide limb angles match the approved adult pose (pose_report: elbow 70, wrist 30, fingers 67-83 breathing, knee 90, ankle 55, toes 37, tail 8-20 deg up). Neck kept in its rest shape, which for the baby is steeper (neck1 ~52 deg vs adult 39) because the neck is short and the head big. Fly wing baseline is +0.05 rad (adult -0.35) and Glide -0.12 rad (adult -0.52) so mean wing elevation matches the adult (8 deg / -2 deg); flap amplitude 0.8 rad as the adult. Runtime dive-tuck overlay on wing1/wing2/fing1 should work unchanged. Mesh edits vs raw Tripo output: tail shortened along x (x<0.04 compressed to 0.5x with a 0.07 blend; Tripo had made the tail 56% of body length with a club as long as the torso), and two inside-out 18-face shells at the wing trailing roots were flipped (they showed as big black patches with the back-face outline). Only the base-colour texture is kept (1024 WEBP q85, EXT_texture_webp); metallic 0 / roughness 0.8, no ORM or normal map, so a MeshStandardMaterial fallback looks flatter than the adult's. Region thresholds (rig_fire_baby.py): head x>0.345 & z>0.05 & |y|<0.125; wing |y|>0.085 & z>-0.015 & x>0.20; legs z<-0.03 & |y|>0.015, front x>0.205 else hind; wing1 also on torso where |y|>0.06 & z>-0.02 & 0.20<x<0.31.
